before_times: Which exam, as your doctor's order says it? Do you have the order, or is your doctor sending it?
Will a plan pay? Just its name here.
For MRI: do you have a pacemaker, defibrillator, nerve stimulator, cochlear implant, pump, aneurysm clip, or metal in your body or eyes? Yes or no here; details on the secure page.
Weight over 350 pounds? (the table's limit; a wider machine elsewhere)
For CT or MRI with contrast: have you had a reaction to contrast before? Yes or no here; details on the secure page.
after_time: Anything that helps the visit, like a step-free way in, a wheelchair transfer, or an interpreter.
Would you like a female technologist? (asked before anyone else does the exam; offered where one is free)
secure_page_only: Date of birth; the plan's member number
The MRI safety form: each implant, device or metal, and its card if you have one
Could you be pregnant? Are you breastfeeding? (for anyone who could be)
Allergies, a contrast reaction, kidney disease, diabetes and its medicines
For calming medicine: who drives you home
Who your results go to: your ordering doctor; any other doctor you name
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult for themselves; a parent or legal guardian for a child; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; a care facility for its residents, with the resident's or agent's consent on file; a doctor's office for its patient.

stop.words: chest pain, trouble breathing, a stroke sign, a bad fall or injury now
stop.say: Call 911 now. Don't come in for an X-ray.

go_on.words: a pacemaker or other implant, or metal in the body
go_on.what: not booked for MRI until the MRI safety technologist reads the form and the implant card; some are never scanned here
X-ray and CT wait for the ordering doctor's word; MRI contrast isn't given; the technologist asks again at the visit
the radiologist OKs it first; any medicine to take before comes from the patient's own doctor
a calming medicine only from the patient's own doctor, and then a driver home

first_steps_and_forms.prep: On a secure link: fasting or a full bladder as the exam needs; no metal or jewelry for MRI; no deodorant for a mammogram; the order, a photo ID and the plan card; a driver if calming medicine is taken.

required.name: The doctor's order
required.when: by the day before (or at the desk for a walk-in X-ray)
required.who: the ordering doctor's office sends it to the center
required.goodFor: the time the order says, often 30 to 90 days
required.result: not in: the desk calls the doctor's office; still not in, the visit can't go ahead

required.name: The plan's prior approval
required.when: before the visit, where the plan requires one for CT or MRI
required.who: the ordering doctor's office or the center's desk
required.result: not approved by the day before: self-pay price with the patient's yes, or a move with no fee

required.name: MRI safety form
required.who: the patient, on the secure page; read by the MRI safety technologist
required.result: OK, No (never scanned here), or Need more (the implant card)

required.name: Kidney blood test
required.when: within 30 days before a contrast exam, for those who need it
required.who: the patient's doctor or a lab

required.name: An X-ray of the eyes before MRI
required.when: before the MRI, for anyone who has worked with metal

staff.skills: each technologist's kinds of exam, as the center lists them
staff.supervision: A contrast exam is offered only while a supervising radiologist or doctor is on site.
staff.who_oks: The MRI safety technologist reads every MRI safety form; the radiologist OKs a past contrast reaction.
staff.stand_in: Another technologist with the same skill. A patient who asked for a female technologist is asked before anyone else does the exam; nobody moves on silence.
staff.roles: Radiologic technologists, CT and MRI technologists, sonographers, mammography technologists, an MRI safety technologist, radiologists (reading and supervising), front desk.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult for themselves; a parent or legal guardian for a child; a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; a care facility for its residents, with the resident's or agent's consent on file; a doctor's office for its patient.
children_and_age.minors_texts: A parent or guardian books; texts go to them.

visit.check_in: The code at the desk. A walk-in X-ray: a place in the line with the order. Mobile: the code at the door, or the facility's nurse at the front desk.
visit.done: The code, or DONE when the images are taken.
visit.changes_at_visit: An exam the order doesn't name is never added; a new or changed order comes from the doctor first.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Optional, and nothing is required by Rosie. The center may list its own records on its page: each machine's state registration, the federal mammography certificate, accreditations, and each technologist's credential and the supervising radiologist. Rosie shows what the center enters, as given.
license.who: The center (its machines and certificates); each technologist; each radiologist.
license.ask: Optional: each machine's registration and end date; the mammography certificate; accreditations; each technologist's credential; the supervising radiologists' names.
license.insurance: Optional: the center may list its malpractice or liability insurance; Rosie does not check it.
license.background: The center's own choice; Rosie does not run one.

never_in_a_text: The exam, the body part, the order's reason, pregnancy, implants, contrast, results. Texts name only the center, the date, the time and the place; staff and owner texts use initials and a secure link.
languages: English and Spanish, plus the center's interpreter line.
